# HerbBlueMap

> HerbBlueMap (herbbluemap.com) is the blueprint of Chinese herbal wisdom in plain English, written for people who use natural remedies and adaptogens but know little about Chinese medicine. It explains the system behind the herbs — which herb, for whom, and when — and offers free interactive tools. Educational content only: no diagnosis, no prescriptions, no cure claims.

## Tools

- [Body Relief — Tung Point Finder](https://herbbluemap.com/body-relief/): A symptom-first interactive atlas of Master Tung acupuncture points for pain. Pick where it hurts (head pain, neck pain, low back pain, sciatica); the map shows the points practitioners use, drawn on body templates, with the classical reasoning for each. Its premise: "Pain doesn't always start where it hurts."

## Herb Library

- [Shennong Bencao Jing Essentials — the Classical 32](https://herbbluemap.com/bencao/): The 32 core herbs of the classical Chinese formulary (the herbs Zhang Zhongjing's formulas run on), distilled from the Shennong Bencao Jing (Divine Farmer's Classic of Materia Medica, ~2,000 years old). One page per herb with a classical plate illustration, the original Chinese text with English translation, flavor/nature/channel entry, a systems-biology reading of its pharmacology, and its classical formula pairings. Herbs: Guizhi (cinnamon twig), Mahuang (ephedra), Fuzi (aconite), Banxia (pinellia), Gegen (kudzu root), Shaoyao (peony root), Gancao (licorice root), Zhigancao (honey-fried licorice), Dazao (jujube), Shengjiang (fresh ginger), Shigao (gypsum), Xingren (apricot kernel), Fuling (poria), Dahuang (rhubarb root), Mangxiao (mirabilite), Xixin (asarum), Huangqin (scutellaria root), Huanglian (coptis root), Zexie (water plantain), Zhuling (polyporus), Zhizi (gardenia fruit), Zhimu (anemarrhena root), Huangqi (astragalus root), Baizhu (atractylodes root), Renshen (ginseng root), Zhishi (immature bitter orange), Houpo (magnolia bark), Wuweizi (schisandra berry), Chaihu (bupleurum root), Danggui (angelica root), Ejiao (donkey-hide gelatin), Chuanxiong (Sichuan lovage rhizome). Each herb page lives at https://herbbluemap.com/bencao/{pinyin}.html — e.g. https://herbbluemap.com/bencao/gancao.html for licorice root. A Chinese edition of the same library is at tcmus.net/tcm/bencao/.

## Guides

- [Adaptogens, the Chinese Originals](https://herbbluemap.com/chinese-herbal-medicine/): Why half the adaptogen shelf (ginseng, astragalus, reishi, schisandra, cordyceps, goji) is classical Chinese medicine in disguise — and how the Chinese system uses them differently: pattern before herb, tonics have temperatures, and almost never alone.
- [Dampness](https://herbbluemap.com/dampness/): The classical Chinese pattern name for the heavy, foggy, sluggish, "tests are normal" feeling — its causes in the classical model (climate, diet, overwork), the drainage/transport metaphor, and the classical playbook. A pattern concept, not a diagnosis.
- [The Chinese Body Clock](https://herbbluemap.com/body-clock/): The twelve two-hour organ shifts (zi wu liu zhu) in plain English, a full table, why 3 a.m. is the classic waking hour (liver shift 1–3 hands over to lung 3–5), three rules for using the clock, and when night waking is a medical question instead.
- [Tongue Reading](https://herbbluemap.com/tongue-diagnosis/): The tongue as a dashboard — the four dials practitioners read (body color, body shape, coating color, coating texture), a chart of classical readings, a 60-second self-reading method, and the limits of the method.
- [Chinese Herbs for Beginners](https://herbbluemap.com/chinese-herbs-for-beginners/): A learning roadmap in the classical order: one idea (hot/cold patterns), the kitchen shelf (ginger, jujube, licorice, goji), the famous tonics in context, the Classical 32 as the original syllabus, then thinking in formulas.
- [Shang Han Lun for Beginners](https://herbbluemap.com/shang-han-lun/): An introduction to Zhang Zhongjing's 1,800-year-old Treatise on Cold Damage — the six stages in plain English, the pattern-before-formula principle, and a free interactive formula finder (Taiyang + Yangming stages) embedded on the page.

## Find a Practitioner

- [Find a Verified Acupuncturist](https://herbbluemap.com/find/): A searchable directory (ZIP + radius, concern, name) of acupuncturists whose licenses were verified one by one against official New York State records (NYSED). Inclusion requires: license confirmed, registration current, and no disciplinary record of any kind, ever. Specialties are practitioner-reported and labeled as such. Coverage: Flushing, Manhattan, Buffalo, Rochester, Syracuse (New York). The same database powers the Chinese-language directory at tcmus.net/find/.
